newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-SPARKLING BRIVE CELEBRATE IN STYLE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SPARKLING BRIVE CELEBRATE IN STYLE.

text.p: Brive maintained the French grip on rugby union's European Cup with a sparkling 28-9 demolition of English opponents Leicester in the final on Saturday.
Roared on by several thousand passionate supporters who made the trip from central France to Cardiff, Brive scored four fine tries and could have won by an even wider margin with better goalkicking.

Flying winger Sebastien Carrat, the tournament's leading try-scorer, added to his growing reputation with two tries after Sebastien Viars and Gerald Fabre had each demonstrated power and pace to register classy scores of their own.
There was only a brief moment early in the second-half when Brive looked in any danger of missing out on the celebratory party which was in full swing within seconds of the final whistle.

A third John Liley penalty had given Leicester a 9-8 lead and their forwards were beginning to exert some pressure on their French counterparts, only for winger Fabre to recapture the lead instantly with a muscular burst down the right touchline.

It was similar in style to Brive's opening points inside the first five minutes when Viars scored a memorable individual try from 50 metres out, bouncing off at least three defenders to set a steamed-up Brive side on their way.

They went off the boil either side of half-time but the moment Carrat, who almost made the French Olympic sprint team and can run the 100 metres in 10.35 seconds, completed a deft handling move in the 63rd minute the outcome was assured.
Lamaison added a drop-goal and right at the end converted Carrat's 10th try of the tournament via an upright, sparking scenes which startled even long-time visitors to Cardiff.

Captain Alain Penaud, who had to be helped off the field in the closing stages, was fit enough to collect the impressive silver trophy and the din of the triumphant brass bands will ring in the ears of Leicester's Australian coach Bob Dwyer for days.
The game was watched by a crowd of 40,664, almost double the number who attended Toulouse's victory over Cardiff in the tournament's inaugural final on the same ground last season.

Brive - 15-Sebastien Viars; 14-Gerald Fabre, 13-Christophe Lamaison, 12-David Venditti, 11-Sebastien Carrat; 10-Alain Penaud (captain) (17-Romauld Paillat, 71st), 9-Phiippe Carbonneau; 8-Francois Duboisset (19-Thierry Labrousse, 49th), 7-Gregori Kacala, 6-Loic van der Linden (22-Yann Domi, 79th), 5-Grant Ross, 4-Eric Allegret (20-Tony Rees, 67th), 3-Richard Crespy, 2-Laurent Travers, 1-Didier Casadei (21-Eric Bouti, 71st).

Leicester - O-John Liley; N-Steve Hackney, M-Will Greenwood, L-Stuart Potter, K-Rory Underwood; J-Rob Liley, I-Austin Healey; G-Dean Richards (captain) (S-Eric Miller, 67th), H-Neil Back, F-John Wells, E-Matt Poole, D-Martin Johnson, C-Darren Garforth, B-Richard Cockerill, A-Graham Rowntree.
